beats.intro: Chapter sixty-three. [[sub]]When a quadratic is just something squared equals a number, you can undo the square directly.
beats.two: Solve x squared equals nine. [[ask]]Which numbers squared give nine? [[pos]]Three, [[neg]]and also negative three. [[graph]]On a graph, the parabola y equals x squared meets the line y equals nine at two points: x equals three and x equals negative three. [[pm]]So the solution is x equals plus or minus three. [[prop]]This is the square root property: if x squared equals b, then x equals plus or minus the square root of b. [[warn]]The radical sign alone gives only the positive root, so the plus or minus has to be written in.
beats.slide: The number on the right decides how many solutions there are. [[move]]Slide the line up and down. [[big]]Any positive number gives two solutions, one on each side. [[twenty]]At twenty, they are plus and minus the square root of twenty, which simplifies to two root five. [[zero]]At zero, the line just touches the bottom of the parabola: one solution, x equals zero. [[below]]Below zero, the line misses the parabola completely. No real number squared is negative, so there's no real solution.
beats.q1: Quick check. Solve with the square root property.
beats.iso: First, get the square by itself. [[ex]]Solve three k squared equals forty-eight. [[div]]Only k is squared, so divide both sides by three: k squared equals sixteen. [[root]]Then k equals plus or minus four. [[ex2]]Another one: three times x plus one, squared, minus seven, equals eleven. [[add]]Add seven: three times x plus one, squared, equals eighteen. [[div2]]Divide by three: x plus one, squared, equals six. [[root2]]Take square roots: x plus one equals plus or minus root six. [[ans]]Subtract one: x equals negative one plus or minus root six.
beats.q2: Quick check. Find the first mistake.
beats.binom: When a binomial is squared, the plus or minus gives two separate answers. [[ex]]Solve k plus four, squared, equals nine. [[root]]k plus four equals plus or minus three. [[split]]So k plus four is three, or k plus four is negative three. [[ans]]k is negative one, or negative seven. [[chk]]Check: three squared is nine, and negative three squared is nine too.
beats.wrap: To sum up. [[w1]]First isolate the squared part. [[w2]]Then take the square root of both sides, and write plus or minus. [[w3]]A positive number gives two solutions, zero gives one, and a negative number gives none. [[w4]]Simplify any radical in the answer. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
beats.final3: Last one. How many real solutions?
beats.finish: Well done. That's the end of chapter sixty-three, solving by taking square roots.
